You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
The churn model `churn-hgb-v3` scored an offline validation AUC of 0.805, but 0.656 in its first live month
(`/app/INCIDENT.md`). Its feature pipeline in `/app/churn` already uses only events stamped before each prediction
(`/app/CHANGELOG.md`), yet the live scoring service computed other values for the same predictions. The live service
computes every feature at the moment of a prediction from the warehouse tables as they stand at that moment
(`/app/live/features.py`). The pipeline builds its training table from an extract taken later (`/app/data`, this
brand's warehouse at 2026-03-05T00:00:00Z). The tables are described in `/app/docs/WAREHOUSE.md`, the warehouse's own
records of its job runs and transactions are in `/app/data/_ops/`, and samples of what the live service computed are
in `/app/logs/`.

Fix `python -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>` (run from `/app`) so that, for every row of the
extract's `scoring_points.csv`, each feature is the value the live service would have computed for that customer at
that row's `as_of`, had it been running then against the warehouse as it stood at that moment (exactly the rows and
values committed to it before that moment, in the tables its queries name). This must hold for any extract with the
layout of `/app/data`. Keep every feature of `/app/live/features.py` whose live value the extract determines for every
row; leave out any feature whose live value the extract cannot determine for some rows.

How the result is checked:
- `python3 -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>` is run from a copy of `/app` at another path, as
  an unprivileged user, on extracts of the company's other brands: the same seven CSV files, `_ops/` folder and layout
  as `/app/data`, about the same size and period, with other customers, events and load histories (their own job runs,
  failures and migrations). It must exit with status 0 and write the parquet file. Do not rely on network access, on
  absolute paths into `/app`, or on anything in `/app/data` or `/app/logs`.
- The output must have exactly one row per row of the extract's `scoring_points.csv`, with the columns `customer_id`,
  `as_of` and every kept feature, named as in `/app/live/features.py`. Extra columns, row order and column order do not
  matter, but a column named after a feature that should be left out fails unless all its values are null.
  `customer_id` may be any integer type; `as_of` a timestamp (time-zone aware, or naive meaning UTC) or an ISO 8601
  string; the integer features (`orders_7d`, `orders_30d`, `spend_30d_cents`, `tickets_30d`) any numeric type holding
  whole numbers; a null a parquet null or NaN.
- Every value must equal what the live service would have computed: integer features exactly, other numbers within
  1e-6 plus 1e-9 times the expected value, strings exactly, nulls exactly where the live service would have had no value.
- An extract is also changed in everything the warehouse did not yet hold at some cut time (in any table, whatever the
  date of the event a row records) and the command is run again: every prediction with `as_of` at or before the cut
  must keep the same feature values (within the tolerances above). The changed extract is still a copy of the
  warehouse at the same moment as the original extract, in the same layout; only what the warehouse did not yet hold
  at the cut differs, and its `_ops/` records match it: every record dated before the cut is unchanged, and the later
  records describe the changed extract.
- Each run is stopped after 60 seconds and then fails. The grading container has the same resources as this one
  (2 vCPUs, 4 GiB), and `/app/data` is about the size of the graded extracts, so time a run on it. Graded runs set
  `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`.
- `python -m churn.train` is not graded; it may help to check the work.

Only /app is kept when we grade: folders named `data`, `__pycache__` or `.venv` anywhere under /app are dropped, and the packages already installed are available.

===== INCIDENT =====
# INC-2077: churn-hgb-v3 scores far worse live than in validation

Status: open. Owner: ML platform on-call. Opened 2026-03-04, updated 2026-03-05.

## What happened
- `churn-hgb-v3` is trained on the feature table that the offline pipeline builds (`churn/`, v3 in `CHANGELOG.md`).
  Built from this brand's extract (`data/`, the warehouse at 2026-03-05T00:00:00Z), that table gives
  **offline validation AUC 0.805** in `python -m churn.train` (trained on the predictions before 2025-09-01,
  validated on those of 2025-09-01 to 2025-11-30).
- The model went live on 2026-01-01. The live scoring service computes the features of each request itself, from the
  warehouse at the moment of the request (`live/features.py`). On the 3,415 predictions of January 2026, whose 30-day
  outcomes have all landed in `labels`: **live AUC 0.656**.
- The model and its hyperparameters did not change between validation and launch.

## Tried so far
- Retrained with much stronger regularization and shallower trees (`--l2 50 --max-depth 2`): offline AUC 0.813. The
  offline number did not fall, so this is not ordinary overfitting.
- Compared the live service with `live/features.py` by hand on 200 January requests: the service computes exactly what
  its queries say.
- Pulled a random sample of about 10% of the requests of January 2026, with the values the service computed:
  `logs/live_2026-01_sample.jsonl`, 365 requests, one JSON object per line with `customer_id`, `as_of`, `trigger`, the
  11 `features` and the model's `score`.

## Next step (model team)
`churn-hgb-v4` is to be trained on a feature table that matches what the live service computed for every past
prediction. Every feature whose live value can be matched for every prediction is kept; any feature whose live value
cannot be matched is dropped from v4.

===== CHANGELOG =====
# Changelog: the offline feature pipeline (`churn/`)

## v3 (2025-12-19): the training table of churn-hgb-v3
Fixes INC-2041: in four places, v2 used events stamped at or after the prediction time `t`.
- `windows.py`: the order, spend and ticket windows are `[t - W days, t)` on the exact event timestamps. v2 summed
  whole UTC days, the day of `t` included, so events later on the prediction day were counted.
- `status.py`: the latest snapshot dated before `date(t)`. A snapshot dated D records the status at the end of day D;
  v2 took the customer's latest snapshot in the extract, which is often dated after `t`.
- `impute.py`: a missing `app_minutes_7d` takes the customer's most recent earlier reading only. v2 filled backward
  first, from a later reading.
- `encoding.py`: `te_district` counts only labels whose 30-day window had closed before `t` (`as_of + 30 days < t`),
  for the district and for the prior alike. v2 used every label in the extract, the prediction's own and later ones
  included.

Also in v3:
- `attributes.py` (new): `plan` and `days_since_last_login` from the customer record, the two features of the live
  service that v2 did not build. A last login at or after `t` is ignored (the feature is null then).
- `extract.py` loads the seven tables described in `docs/WAREHOUSE.md`.
- `train.py`: every column of the feature table other than `customer_id` and `as_of` is a model input, and string
  columns are one-hot encoded (v2 encoded `status` only); a column that holds no value at all is skipped.

# Warehouse tables (churn scoring)

Written 2025-02-14 by the data platform for the warehouse and its nightly loaders as they were on that date, and not
updated since. The scheduler's own records of every job run and transaction, later changes included, are in each
extract's `_ops/` folder (below).

The seven tables below are the warehouse tables that the live scoring service (`live/features.py`) and the churn
pipeline (`churn/`) read. This page says what each table holds and which system writes it. Every brand of the company
runs the same warehouse and jobs; each

- Only plan changes are logged (`plan_changes`); no history of `last_login_at` is kept.

### `plan_changes`
`customer_id, changed_at, old_plan, new_plan, _loaded_at`: one row per plan change that `crm_sync` has applied. Each
sync writes one row for every change made in the CRM before its start that no earlier sync applied; `changed_at` is
when the customer made the change in the CRM, `_loaded_at` the commit of the sync that applied it. A customer's rows
are every change applied since sign-up, so the earliest row's `old_plan` is the plan chosen at sign-up. When one sync
applies several changes of a customer, the plan after that sync is the `new_plan` of the latest of them (by
`changed_at`), the CRM's plan at the sync's start.

### `scoring_points`
`customer_id, as_of, trigger, app_minutes_7d`: one row per scoring request, written by the scoring service at the
moment of the request, `as_of`. `trigger` is `batch` (the 06:00 run, which scores a customer every 14 days, on the
customer's billing weekday) or `ticket` (a request the support desk sends when a ticket is opened, for some of the
tickets, at the ticket's `opened_at`). `app_minutes_7d` is the product-analytics reading that came with the request (the customer's minutes in
the app over the last 7 days), empty when the request came without one (analytics export outages, devices offline).
`(customer_id, as_of)` is unique.

### `orders`
`order_id, customer_id, ordered_at, kind, amount_cents, _load_job, _loaded_at`. `kind` is `box` (the weekly box,
charged by billing at 05:30 on the customer's billing weekday; `ordered_at` is the charge) or `addon` (an extra item,
ordered at any time). Each order exists in the order system, which the loaders read, from its `ordered_at` on.
The nightly `legacy_orders` job writes the table: each run selects orders from the order system and sends them to
`orders` in one transaction.

### `tickets`
`ticket_id, customer_id, opened_at, topic, _loaded_at`: support tickets, written by change data capture from the
support desk 1 to 30 seconds after `opened_at`.

### `status_snapshots`
`customer_id, snapshot_date, status, _loaded_at`: the billing system's account status (`active`, `paused`,
`payment_failed` or `cancelled`) at the end of day `snapshot_date`. Billing records a row for a customer on the
sign-up day, on every day the status changed, and on the first day of every month, up to the cancellation (a
`cancelled` row is the customer's last); there is at most one row per customer and date.
`billing_export` writes each day's partition (all the rows dated D) in one transaction.

### `labels`
`customer_id, as_of, churned_30d, _loaded_at`: the outcome of a prediction (`customer_id` and `as_of` as in
`scoring_points`): `churned_30d` is 1 if the customer cancelled in `(as_of, as_of + 30 days]`, else 0. The outcome
becomes known at the cancellation, or when the 30 days have passed without one.
`label_job` writes, in one transaction per run, a row for each prediction whose outcome became known before the run
started and that has no row yet.

"""Build the churn feature table: python -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>"""
import argparse
import os

from churn.attributes import days_since_last_login, plan
from churn.encoding import district_encoding
from churn.extract import load_extract
from churn.impute import fill_app_minutes
from churn.status import latest_status
from churn.windows import activity_features, tenure_days

FEATURE_COLUMNS = ["orders_7d", "orders_30d", "spend_30d_cents", "tickets_30d", "days_since_last_order",
                   "tenure_days", "status", "plan", "days_since_last_login", "app_minutes_7d", "te_district"]


def build(data_dir):
    t = load_extract(data_dir)
    points = t["scoring_points"].reset_index(drop=True)
    feats = activity_features(points, t["orders"], t["tickets"])
    feats["tenure_days"] = tenure_days(points, t["customers"])
    feats["status"] = latest_status(points, t["status_snapshots"])
    feats["plan"] = plan(points, t["customers"])
    feats["days_since_last_login"] = days_since_last_login(points, t["customers"])
    feats["app_minutes_7d"] = fill_app_minutes(points)
    feats["te_district"] = district_encoding(points, t["labels"], t["customers"])
    return feats[["customer_id", "as_of"] + FEATURE_COLUMNS]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--data", required=True, help="folder with the extract CSVs")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output parquet file")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    feats = build(a.data)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(a.out)), exist_ok=True)
    feats.to_parquet(a.out, index=False)
    print(f"wrote {len(feats)} rows x {feats.shape[1]} columns to {a.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    52  are every change applied since sign-up, so the earliest row's `old_plan` is the plan chosen at sign-up. When one sync
    53  applies several changes of a customer, the plan after that sync is the `new_plan` of the latest of them (by
    54  `changed_at`), the CRM's plan at the sync's start.
    55
    56  ### `scoring_points`
    57  `customer_id, as_of, trigger, app_minutes_7d`: one row per scoring request, written by the scoring service at the
    58  moment of the request, `as_of`. `trigger` is `batch` (the 06:00 run, which scores a customer every 14 days, on the
    59  customer's billing weekday) or `ticket` (a request the support desk sends when a ticket is opened, for some of the
    60  tickets, at the ticket's `opened_at`). `app_minutes_7d` is the product-analytics reading that came with the request (the customer's minutes in
    61  the app over the last 7 days), empty when the request came without one (analytics export outages, devices offline).
    62  `(customer_id, as_of)` is unique.
    63
    64  ### `orders`
    65  `order_id, customer_id, ordered_at, kind, amount_cents, _load_job, _loaded_at`. `kind` is `box` (the weekly box,
    66  charged by billing at 05:30 on the customer's billing weekday; `ordered_at` is the charge) or `addon` (an extra item,
    67  ordered at any time). Each order exists in the order system, which the loaders read, from its `ordered_at` on.
    68  The nightly `legacy_orders` job writes the table: each run selects orders from the order system and sends them to
    69  `orders` in one transaction.

    72  `ticket_id, customer_id, opened_at, topic, _loaded_at`: support tickets, written by change data capture from the
    73  support desk 1 to 30 seconds after `opened_at`.
    74
    75  ### `status_snapshots`
    76  `customer_id, snapshot_date, status, _loaded_at`: the billing system's account status (`active`, `paused`,
    77  `payment_failed` or `cancelled`) at the end of day `snapshot_date`. Billing records a row for a customer on the
    78  sign-up day, on every day the status changed, and on the first day of every month, up to the cancellation (a
    79  `cancelled` row is the customer's last); there is at most one row per customer and date.
    80  `billing_export` writes each day's partition (all the rows dated D) in one transaction.

    82  ### `labels`
    83  `customer_id, as_of, churned_30d, _loaded_at`: the outcome of a prediction (`customer_id` and `as_of` as in

Current Terminal Screen:
    10
    11  ## Reading the warehouse
    12  - A query that starts at a moment t sees exactly the rows and values committed before t: a row committed at or after
    13    t is not seen, and a value overwritten at or after t is seen as it was before the overwrite, whatever the date of
    14    the event the row records.
    15  - A query reads each table by the name it has when the query starts.
    16  - `_loaded_at` is the commit time of the load that wrote the row; in `orders`, `_load_job` names that load.
    17  - An extract is a copy of every table as the warehouse held it at one moment: the rows and values committed before
    18    that moment, with the `_ops/` records written before it.
    19  - Timestamps are UTC, written as ISO 8601 with a `Z` suffix and whole seconds (`2025-02-04T06:00:00Z`);
    20    `snapshot_date` is a UTC date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); amounts are integer cents. Columns whose names start with `_` are
    21    written by the loaders, not by the source systems.
    22
    23  ## The scheduler's records (`_ops/`)
    24  - `_ops/scheduler.log` has one UTC event per line, `<time> <job> run=<run> <event>`: each task's start
    25    (`state=running`) and end (`state=success` or `state=failed`), and between them the lines the task writes, such as
    26    the rows it selected or copied, the transaction it sent (`sent txn <n> to commit`), the statements it ran and the
    27    checks it made.
    28  - `_ops/commits.jsonl` has one JSON object per transaction a scheduled job sent: `txn`, `at`, `outcome` (`commit` or
    29    `rollback`), `table` and `rows` (the table the transaction writes rows into and how many; null for schema
    30    statements).
    31  - `_ops/commits.jsonl` is the commit log of the scheduled jobs: a transaction is committed if and only if its outcome
    32    is `commit`, and it is committed at its `at`; the scheduler's task states describe tasks, not commits.
    33  - Change data capture (`tickets`), the sign-up service and the scoring service write without the scheduler and are not
    34    in `_ops/`.
    35
    36  ## Tables
    37
    38  ### `customers`
    39  `customer_id, signup_at, plan, postcode_district, last_login_at, _updated_at`: one row per customer.
    40  - The sign-up service writes the row at `signup_at`: the plan chosen at sign-up (`basic`, `plus` or `family`), the
    41    postcode district, an empty `last_login_at`, and `_updated_at` = `signup_at`. `signup_at` and `postcode_district`
    42    never change.
    43  - `crm_sync` reads the CRM at its start. For each customer whose plan or last login in the CRM (the latest login to
    44    the app or website before the sync's start) differs from the row, it overwrites `plan` and `last_login_at` with the
    45    CRM's values and sets `_updated_at` to the sync's commit time.
    46  - Only plan changes are logged (`plan_changes`); no history of `last_login_at` is kept.

    48  ### `plan_changes`

"""Warehouse visibility metadata reconstructed from an extract's `_ops` records.

Append rows normally become visible at their `_loaded_at`, but a table can be replaced by a
backfill/rename.  A query reads the table *name* which was current when it started, so rows in the
replacement are not visible merely because they were loaded into its old name.
"""
import os
import re
import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

_SELECT_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\S+ legacy_orders run=\S+ selected orders where ordered_at >= (\S+) "
    r"and ordered_at < (\S+): (\d+) rows; sent txn (\d+) to commit into (\S+)$"
)
_STATEMENT_RE = re.compile(
    r"statement:\s*ALTER TABLE\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s+RENAME TO\s+"
    r"([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*$"
)
_TXN_RE = re.compile(r"schema_migrations run=\S+ sent txn (\d+) to commit")


def _committed_transactions(ops_dir):
    path = os.path.join(ops_dir, "commits.jsonl")
    committed = {}
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            row = json.loads(line)
            if row.get("outcome") == "commit" and row.get("at"):
                committed[int(row["txn"])] = pd.to_datetime(row["at"], utc=True)
    return committed


def _orders_rename_commit(ops_dir, committed):
    """Find the last committed schema transaction which renamed another table to `orders`."""
    statements = []
    candidates = []
    with open(os.path.join(ops_dir, "scheduler.log"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            match = _STATEMENT_RE.search(line)
            if match:
                statements.append((match.group(1), match.group(2)))
                continue
            match = _TXN_RE.search(line)
            if match:
                txn = int(match.group(1))
                if any(new_name == "orders" for _old_name, new_name in statements):
                    candidates.append((txn, tuple(statements)))
                statements = []
    for txn, _statements in reversed(candidates):
        at = committed.get(txn)
        if at is not None:
            return at
    return None


def _legacy_intervals(ops_dir, committed, rename_at):
    intervals = []
    with open(os.path.join(ops_dir, "scheduler.log"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            match = _SELECT_RE.match(line.rstrip("\n"))
            if not match:
                continue
            start, end, selected, txn, table = match.groups()
            if table != "orders" or int(selected) == 0:
                continue
            at = committed.get(int(txn))
            if at is not None and at < rename_at:
                intervals.append((pd.Timestamp(start), pd.Timestamp(end), at))
    if not intervals:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["start", "end", "at"])
    result = pd.DataFrame(intervals, columns=["start", "end", "at"])
    # A failed transaction was retried.  The first committed selection of an event interval
    # is the moment those rows became visible in the old table.
    result = result.sort_values(["start", "at"], kind="mergesort")
    result = result.drop_duplicates("start", keep="first")
    return result


def order_commit_times(orders, ops_dir):
    """Effective commit time of each row of the final `orders` table.

    For rows from a replacement table, this accounts for the time before that table was the one
    named `orders`.  Rows selected by the old daily loader use its committed transaction time.
    """
    visible = orders["_loaded_at"].copy()
    rename_at = _orders_rename_commit(ops_dir, _committed_transactions(ops_dir))
    if rename_at is None:
        return visible

    intervals = _legacy_intervals(ops_dir, _committed_transactions(ops_dir), rename_at)
    loaded = orders["_loaded_at"].to_numpy(dtype="datetime64[ns]")
    ordered = orders["ordered_at"].to_numpy(dtype="datetime64[ns]")
    rename = rename_at.to_datetime64()
    pre_rename = ordered < rename

    if intervals.empty:
        visible.iloc[pre_rename] = np.maximum(loaded[pre_rename], rename)
        return pd.to_datetime(visible, utc=True)

    starts = intervals["start"].to_numpy(dtype="datetime64[ns]")
    ends = intervals["end"].to_numpy(dtype="datetime64[ns]")
    commit = intervals["at"].to_numpy(dtype="datetime64[ns]")
    pos = np.searchsorted(starts, ordered[pre_rename], side="right") - 1
    clipped = np.clip(pos, 0, len(starts) - 1)
    known = (pos >= 0) & (ordered[pre_rename] < ends[clipped])
    old_commit = commit[clipped]
    replacement_commit = np.maximum(loaded[pre_rename], rename)
    visible.iloc[pre_rename] = np.where(known, old_commit, replacement_commit)
    return pd.to_datetime(visible, utc=True)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")


def _seconds(values):

    orders_30d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    spend = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    tickets_30d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    last_order_days = np.full(n, np.nan, dtype="float64")

        frame = frame.sort_values(["customer_id", event_col], kind="mergesort")
        groups = {}
        for cid, group in frame.groupby("customer_id", sort=False):
            times = group[event_col].to_numpy(dtype="datetime64[ns]")
            loads = group["_effective_loaded_at"].to_numpy(dtype="datetime64[ns]")
            if "amount_cents" in group:

            else:

            groups[int(cid)] = (times, loads, amounts)
        return groups

    ticket_groups = event_groups(tickets, "opened_at")

        t = _timestamp(at)
        group = order_groups.get(int(cid))
        if group is not None:
            times, loads, amounts = group
            hi = np.searchsorted(times, t, side="left")
            if hi:
                seen = loads[:hi] < t
                if seen.any():
                    event = times[:hi][seen]
                    amounts_seen = amounts[:hi][seen]
                    orders_7d[i] = np.count_nonzero(event >= t - np.timedelta64(7, "D"))
                    orders_30d[i] = np.count_nonzero(event >= t - np.timedelta64(30, "D"))
                    spend[i] = int(np.nansum(amounts_seen[event >= t - np.timedelta64(30, "D")]))
                    last_order_days[i] = (at - pd.Timestamp(event[-1], tz="UTC")).total_seconds() / 86400.0

        group = ticket_groups.get(int(cid))
        if group is not None:
            times, loads, _amounts = group
            hi = np.searchsorted(times, t, side="left")
            if hi:
                seen = loads[:hi] < t
                if seen.any():
                    event = times[:hi][seen]
                    tickets_30d[i] = np.count_nonzero(event >= t - np.timedelta64(30, "D"))

    out = points[["customer_id", "as_of"]].copy()
    out["orders_7d"] = orders_7d
    out["orders_30d"] = orders_30d
    out["spend_30d_cents"] = spend
    out["tickets_30d"] = tickets_30d
    out["days_since_last_order"] = last_order_days
    return out


def tenure_days(points, customers):
    signup = points["customer_id"].map(customers.set_index("customer_id")["signup_at"])

"""Latest account status visible to the live warehouse query."""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10


def _seconds(values):
    return ((values - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def latest_status(points, snapshots):
    """Snapshot with the latest date among rows whose load committed before the prediction."""
    loaded = _seconds(snapshots["_loaded_at"])
    event = snapshots["snapshot_date"].astype("int64").to_numpy()
    key = snapshots["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64") * STRIDE + loaded
    order = np.argsort(key, kind="mergesort")
    key = key[order]
    event = event[order]
    status = snapshots["status"].to_numpy(dtype=object)[order]

    running_max = np.maximum.accumulate(event)
    changed = np.r_[True, running_max[1:] != running_max[:-1]]
    best_status = pd.Series(status, index=snapshots.index).where(changed).ffill().to_numpy(dtype=object)

    point_key = points["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64") * STRIDE + _seconds(points["as_of"])
    pos = np.searchsorted(key, point_key, side="left")
    result = np.full(len(points), None, dtype=object)
    known = pos > 0
    result[known] = best_status[pos[known] - 1]
    return pd.Series(result, index=points.index, dtype="object")

"""Customer attributes that can be reconstructed historically."""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10


def _seconds(values):
    return ((values - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def plan(points, plan_changes, customers):
    """Plan on the customer record at each prediction, reconstructed from plan changes."""
    current = customers.set_index("customer_id")["plan"]
    histories = {}
    if not plan_changes.empty:
        changes = plan_changes.copy()
        changes["commit"] = _seconds(changes["_loaded_at"])
        first = changes.sort_values(["customer_id", "changed_at"], kind="mergesort")
        initial = first.groupby("customer_id", sort=False).first()["old_plan"]
        for cid, group in changes.groupby("customer_id", sort=False):
            base = initial.loc[cid]
            if pd.isna(base):
                base = current.get(cid)
            group = group.sort_values(["commit", "changed_at"], kind="mergesort")
            best_changed = None
            best_plan = base
            commit_times = []
            plan_values = []
            for commit, rows in group.groupby("commit", sort=True):
                for changed_at, new_plan in zip(rows["changed_at"].to_numpy(), rows["new_plan"].to_numpy()):
                    if best_changed is None or changed_at > best_changed:
                        best_changed = changed_at
                        best_plan = new_plan
                commit_times.append(int(commit))
                plan_values.append(best_plan)
            histories[int(cid)] = (base, np.asarray(commit_times, dtype="int64"), plan_values)

    result = np.full(len(points), None, dtype=object)
    for i, (cid, at) in enumerate(zip(points["customer_id"].to_numpy(), points["as_of"].to_numpy())):
        cid = int(cid)
        if cid not in current.index:
            continue
        if cid not in histories:
            value = current.loc[cid]
            result[i] = None if pd.isna(value) else value
            continue
        base, commits, values = histories[cid]
        pos = np.searchsorted(commits, _seconds(pd.Series([at]))[0], side="left")
        result[i] = base if pos == 0 else values[pos - 1]
    return pd.Series(result, index=points.index, dtype="object")


def days_since_last_login(points, customers):
    """Kept only as null in the offline table: login history is not in the warehouse extract."""
    return pd.Series(np.nan, index=points.index, dtype="float64")

"""Point-in-time smoothed district target encoding."""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10


def _seconds(values):
    return ((values - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def district_encoding(points, labels, customers, m=20):
    """Reproduce the live SQL using label rows committed before each prediction."""
    districts = customers.set_index("customer_id")["postcode_district"]
    lab = labels.copy()
    lab["postcode_district"] = lab["customer_id"].map(districts)
    lab = lab[lab["postcode_district"].notna()].copy()

    all_districts = pd.concat([lab["postcode_district"], points["customer_id"].map(districts)], ignore_index=True)
    codes = all_districts.astype("category").cat.codes.to_numpy()
    lab_codes = codes[:len(lab)]
    point_codes = codes[len(lab):]

    y = pd.to_numeric(lab["churned_30d"], errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype="float64")
    y_sum = np.nancumsum(y)
    y_seen = np.cumsum(~np.isnan(y))
    n_rows = np.arange(1, len(lab) + 1, dtype="int64")

    loaded = _seconds(lab["_loaded_at"])
    order = np.argsort(loaded, kind="mergesort")
    global_load = loaded[order]
    global_sum = y_sum[order]
    global_seen = y_seen[order]
    global_rows = n_rows[order]

    key = lab_codes.astype("int64") * STRIDE + loaded
    order2 = np.argsort(key, kind="mergesort")
    district_key = key[order2]
    district_sum = y_sum[order2]
    district_rows = n_rows[order2]

    t = _seconds(points["as_of"])
    gp = np.searchsorted(global_load, t, side="left")
    global_n = np.where(gp > 0, global_rows[np.maximum(gp - 1, 0)], 0)
    global_s = np.where(gp > 0, global_sum[np.maximum(gp - 1, 0)], 0.0)
    global_seen_n = np.where(gp > 0, global_seen[np.maximum(gp - 1, 0)], 0)
    prior = np.full(len(points), 0.05, dtype="float64")
    has_prior = global_seen_n > 0
    prior[has_prior] = global_s[has_prior] / global_seen_n[has_prior]

    point_key = point_codes.astype("int64") * STRIDE + t
    hp = np.searchsorted(district_key, point_key, side="left")
    n = np.where(hp > 0, district_rows[np.maximum(hp - 1, 0)], 0)
    s = np.where(hp > 0, district_sum[np.maximum(hp - 1, 0)], 0.0)
    return pd.Series((s + m * prior) / (n + m), index=points.index, dtype="float64")

"""Warehouse visibility metadata reconstructed from an extract's `_ops` records.

Append rows normally become visible at their `_loaded_at`, but a table can be replaced by a
backfill and rename.  A query reads the table *name* which was current when it started, so rows in
the replacement are not visible merely because they were loaded into its old name.
"""
import os
import re
import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

_SELECT_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\S+ legacy_orders run=\S+ selected orders where ordered_at >= (\S+) "
    r"and ordered_at < (\S+): (\d+) rows; sent txn (\d+) to commit into (\S+)$"
)
_STATEMENT_RE = re.compile(
    r"statement:\s*ALTER TABLE\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s+RENAME TO\s+"
    r"([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*$"
)
_TXN_RE = re.compile(r"schema_migrations run=\S+ sent txn (\d+) to commit")


def _committed_transactions(ops_dir):
    path = os.path.join(ops_dir, "commits.jsonl")
    committed = {}
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            row = json.loads(line)
            if row.get("outcome") == "commit" and row.get("at"):
                committed[int(row["txn"])] = pd.to_datetime(row["at"], utc=True)
    return committed


def _orders_rename_commit(ops_dir, committed):
    """Find a committed schema transaction which renamed another table to `orders`."""
    statements = []
    candidates = []
    with open(os.path.join(ops_dir, "scheduler.log"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            match = _STATEMENT_RE.search(line)
            if match:
                statements.append((match.group(1), match.group(2)))
                continue
            match = _TXN_RE.search(line)
            if match:
                txn = int(match.group(1))
                if any(new_name == "orders" for _old_name, new_name in statements):
                    candidates.append((txn, tuple(statements)))
                statements = []
    for txn, _statements in reversed(candidates):
        at = committed.get(txn)
        if at is not None:
            return at
    return None


def _legacy_intervals(ops_dir, committed, rename_at):
    """Committed event intervals loaded into the old table named `orders`."""
    intervals = []
    with open(os.path.join(ops_dir, "scheduler.log"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            match = _SELECT_RE.match(line.rstrip("\n"))
            if not match:
                continue
            start, end, selected, txn, table = match.groups()
            if table != "orders" or int(selected) == 0:
                continue
            at = committed.get(int(txn))
            if at is not None and at < rename_at:
                intervals.append((pd.Timestamp(start).value, pd.Timestamp(end).value, at.value))
    if not intervals:
        return np.empty((0, 3), dtype="int64")
    result = pd.DataFrame(intervals, columns=["start", "end", "at"])
    # A failed transaction was retried.  The first committed selection of an event interval
    # is the moment those rows became visible in the old table.
    result = result.sort_values(["start", "at"], kind="mergesort")
    result = result.drop_duplicates("start", keep="first")
    return result[["start", "end", "at"]].to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def order_commit_times(orders, ops_dir):
    """Effective commit time of each row of the final `orders` table."""
    rename_at = _orders_rename_commit(ops_dir, _committed_transactions(ops_dir))
    if rename_at is None:
        return orders["_loaded_at"].copy()

    loaded = orders["_loaded_at"].astype("int64").to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    ordered = orders["ordered_at"].astype("int64").to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    rename = int(rename_at.value)
    intervals = _legacy_intervals(ops_dir, _committed_transactions(ops_dir), rename_at)

    visible = loaded.copy()
    pre_rename = ordered < rename
    if not pre_rename.any() or len(intervals) == 0:
        visible[pre_rename] = np.maximum(loaded[pre_rename], rename)
        return pd.Series(pd.to_datetime(visible, utc=True), index=orders.index)

    starts = intervals[:, 0]
    ends = intervals[:, 1]
    commit = intervals[:, 2]
    pos = np.searchsorted(starts, ordered[pre_rename], side="right") - 1
    clipped = np.clip(pos, 0, len(starts) - 1)
    known = (pos >= 0) & (ordered[pre_rename] < ends[clipped])
    old_commit = commit[clipped]
    replacement_commit = np.maximum(loaded[pre_rename], rename)
    visible[pre_rename] = np.where(known, old_commit, replacement_commit)
    return pd.Series(pd.to_datetime(visible, utc=True), index=orders.index)

"""Latest account status visible to the live warehouse query."""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10


def _seconds(values):
    return ((values - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def latest_status(points, snapshots):
    """Snapshot with the latest date among rows whose load committed before each prediction."""
    event = snapshots["snapshot_date"].astype("int64").to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    loaded = _seconds(snapshots["_loaded_at"])
    customer = snapshots["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    key = customer * STRIDE + loaded
    order = np.argsort(key, kind="mergesort")
    customer = customer[order]
    event = event[order]
    status = snapshots["status"].to_numpy(dtype=object)[order]

    # Reset the running maximum of snapshot date at every customer boundary.
    running_max = np.empty(len(event), dtype=event.dtype)
    previous = None
    current_max = None
    for i, (cid, value) in enumerate(zip(customer, event)):
        if cid != previous:
            current_max = value
            previous = cid
        elif value > current_max:
            current_max = value
        running_max[i] = current_max
    changed = np.r_[True, running_max[1:] != running_max[:-1]]
    best_status = pd.Series(status, index=snapshots.index).where(changed).ffill().to_numpy(dtype=object)

    point_key = points["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64") * STRIDE + _seconds(points["as_of"])
    pos = np.searchsorted(key, point_key, side="left")
    result = np.full(len(points), None, dtype=object)
    known = pos > 0
    result[known] = best_status[pos[known] - 1]
    return pd.Series(result, index=points.index, dtype="object")

"""Point-in-time smoothed district target encoding."""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10


def _seconds(values):
    return ((values - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def district_encoding(points, labels, customers, m=20):
    """Reproduce the live SQL using label rows committed before each prediction."""
    districts = customers.set_index("customer_id")["postcode_district"]
    lab = labels.copy()
    lab["postcode_district"] = lab["customer_id"].map(districts)
    lab = lab[lab["postcode_district"].notna()].copy()

    all_districts = pd.concat(
        [lab["postcode_district"], points["customer_id"].map(districts)], ignore_index=True
    )
    codes = all_districts.astype("category").cat.codes.to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    lab_codes = codes[:len(lab)]
    point_codes = codes[len(lab):]

    y = pd.to_numeric(lab["churned_30d"], errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype="float64")
    valid = ~np.isnan(y)
    y_filled = np.where(valid, y, 0.0)

    # Global prior: cumulative sum and non-null count by commit time.
    loaded = _seconds(lab["_loaded_at"])
    order = np.argsort(loaded, kind="mergesort")
    global_load = loaded[order]
    global_sum = np.cumsum(y_filled[order])
    global_count = np.cumsum(valid[order]).astype("int64")
    global_rows = np.arange(1, len(lab) + 1, dtype="int64")[order]

    # District numerator/denominator: cumulative values reset at each district boundary.
    key = lab_codes.astype("int64") * STRIDE + loaded
    order2 = np.argsort(key, kind="mergesort")
    district_key = key[order2]
    district_sorted = lab_codes[order2]
    district_sum = np.cumsum(y_filled[order2])
    district_count = np.cumsum(valid[order2]).astype("int64")
    district_rows = np.empty(len(lab), dtype="int64")
    previous = None
    count = 0
    for i, cid in enumerate(district_sorted):
        if cid != previous:
            count = 0
            previous = cid
        count += 1
        district_rows[i] = count

    t = _seconds(points["as_of"])
    gp = np.searchsorted(global_load, t, side="left")
    global_n = np.where(gp > 0, global_rows[np.maximum(gp - 1, 0)], 0)
    global_s = np.where(gp > 0, global_sum[np.maximum(gp - 1, 0)], 0.0)
    global_seen = np.where(gp > 0, global_count[np.maximum(gp - 1, 0)], 0)
    prior = np.full(len(points), 0.05, dtype="float64")
    has_prior = global_seen > 0
    prior[has_prior] = global_s[has_prior] / global_seen[has_prior]

    point_key = point_codes.astype("int64") * STRIDE + t
    hp = np.searchsorted(district_key, point_key, side="left")
    district_n = np.where(hp > 0, district_rows[np.maximum(hp - 1, 0)], 0)
    district_s = np.where(hp > 0, district_sum[np.maximum(hp - 1, 0)], 0.0)
    return pd.Series((district_s + m * prior) / (district_n + m), index=points.index, dtype="float64")

"""Latest account status visible to the live warehouse query."""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10


def _seconds(values):
    return ((values - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def latest_status(points, snapshots):
    """Snapshot with the latest date among rows whose load committed before each prediction."""
    event = snapshots["snapshot_date"].to_numpy(dtype="datetime64[ns]").astype("int64")
    loaded = _seconds(snapshots["_loaded_at"])
    customer = snapshots["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    key = customer * STRIDE + loaded
    order = np.argsort(key, kind="mergesort")
    customer = customer[order]
    event = event[order]
    status = snapshots["status"].to_numpy(dtype=object)[order]

    # The best status is a running maximum of snapshot date, resetting for each customer.
    running_max = np.empty(len(event), dtype=event.dtype)
    previous = None
    current_max = None
    for i, (cid, value) in enumerate(zip(customer, event)):
        if cid != previous:
            current_max = value
            previous = cid
        elif value > current_max:
            current_max = value
        running_max[i] = current_max
    changed = np.r_[True, running_max[1:] != running_max[:-1]]
    best_status = pd.Series(status).where(changed).ffill().to_numpy(dtype=object)

    point_key = points["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64") * STRIDE + _seconds(points["as_of"])
    pos = np.searchsorted(key, point_key, side="left")
    result = np.full(len(points), None, dtype=object)
    known = pos > 0
    result[known] = best_status[pos[known] - 1]
    return pd.Series(result, index=points.index, dtype="object")

"""Point-in-time smoothed district target encoding."""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10


def _seconds(values):
    return ((values - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def district_encoding(points, labels, customers, m=20):
    """Reproduce the live SQL using label rows committed before each prediction."""
    districts = customers.set_index("customer_id")["postcode_district"]
    lab = labels.copy()
    lab["postcode_district"] = lab["customer_id"].map(districts)
    lab = lab[lab["postcode_district"].notna()].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

    all_districts = pd.concat(
        [lab["postcode_district"], points["customer_id"].map(districts)], ignore_index=True
    )
    codes = all_districts.astype("category").cat.codes.to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    lab_codes = codes[:len(lab)]
    point_codes = codes[len(lab):]

    y = pd.to_numeric(lab["churned_30d"], errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype="float64")
    y_filled = np.nan_to_num(y, nan=0.0)
    raw_sum = np.cumsum(y_filled)
    raw_rows = np.arange(1, len(lab) + 1, dtype="int64")

    loaded = _seconds(lab["_loaded_at"])

    # Global prior from all label rows visible at the prediction time.
    global_order = np.argsort(loaded, kind="mergesort")
    global_load = loaded[global_order]
    global_sum = raw_sum[global_order]
    global_rows = raw_rows[global_order]

    # District statistics are cumulative only within that district.
    key = lab_codes.astype("int64") * STRIDE + loaded
    order = np.argsort(key, kind="mergesort")
    district_key = key[order]
    district_order = lab_codes[order]
    boundaries = np.r_[True, district_order[1:] != district_order[:-1]]
    starts = np.flatnonzero(boundaries)
    previous_start = np.maximum(starts - 1, -1)
    group_start_for_row = np.repeat(starts, np.diff(np.r_[starts, len(lab)]))
    previous_before_group = np.where(group_start_for_row == 0, -1, group_start_for_row - 1)
    district_sum = raw_sum[order] - np.where(previous_before_group >= 0, raw_sum[order][previous_before_group], 0.0)
    district_rows = raw_rows[order] - np.where(previous_before_group >= 0, raw_rows[order][previous_before_group], 0)

    t = _seconds(points["as_of"])
    gp = np.searchsorted(global_load, t, side="left")
    global_n = np.where(gp > 0, global_rows[np.maximum(gp - 1, 0)], 0)
    global_s = np.where(gp > 0, global_sum[np.maximum(gp - 1, 0)], 0.0)
    prior = np.where(global_n > 0, global_s / np.maximum(global_n, 1), 0.05)

    point_key = point_codes.astype("int64") * STRIDE + t
    hp = np.searchsorted(district_key, point_key, side="left")
    n = np.where(hp > 0, district_rows[np.maximum(hp - 1, 0)], 0)
    s = np.where(hp > 0, district_sum[np.maximum(hp - 1, 0)], 0.0)
    return pd.Series((s + m * prior) / (n + m), index=points.index, dtype="float64")

import pandas as pd

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10

    return ((values - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")

    lab = lab[lab["postcode_district"].notna()].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

    all_districts = pd.concat(
        [lab["postcode_district"], points["customer_id"].map(districts)], ignore_index=True
    )
    codes = all_districts.astype("category").cat.codes.to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    lab_codes = codes[:len(lab)]
    point_codes = codes[len(lab):]

    y = pd.to_numeric(lab["churned_30d"], errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype="float64")
    valid = ~np.isnan(y)
    y_filled = np.nan_to_num(y, nan=0.0)
    rows = np.arange(1, len(lab) + 1, dtype="int64")

    # Global prior: all label rows visible to the query at time t.
    loaded = _seconds(lab["_loaded_at"])
    global_order = np.argsort(loaded, kind="mergesort")
    global_load = loaded[global_order]
    global_sum = np.cumsum(y_filled[global_order])
    global_rows = rows[global_order]
    global_seen = np.cumsum(valid[global_order]).astype("int64")

    # District statistics: cumulative values reset at each district group.
    key = lab_codes.astype("int64") * STRIDE + loaded
    order = np.argsort(key, kind="mergesort")
    district_key = key[order]
    district_codes = lab_codes[order]
    starts = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, district_codes[1:] != district_codes[:-1]])
    group_ends = np.r_[starts[1:], len(lab)]
    group_start_sum = np.where(starts == 0, 0.0, np.cumsum(y_filled[order])[starts - 1])
    group_start_rows = np.where(starts == 0, 0, rows[order][starts - 1])
    cumulative_sum = np.cumsum(y_filled[order])
    cumulative_rows = rows[order]
    district_sum = cumulative_sum - np.repeat(group_start_sum, group_ends - starts)
    district_rows = cumulative_rows - np.repeat(group_start_rows, group_ends - starts)

    t = _seconds(points["as_of"])
    gp = np.searchsorted(global_load, t, side="left")
    global_n = np.where(gp > 0, global_rows[np.maximum(gp - 1, 0)], 0)
    global_s = np.where(gp > 0, global_sum[np.maximum(gp - 1, 0)], 0.0)
    global_count = np.where(gp > 0, global_seen[np.maximum(gp - 1, 0)], 0)
    prior = np.full(len(points), 0.05, dtype="float64")
    has_prior = global_count > 0
    prior[has_prior] = global_s[has_prior] / global_count[has_prior]

    point_key = point_codes.astype("int64") * STRIDE + t
    hp = np.searchsorted(district_key, point_key, side="left")
    n = np.where(hp > 0, district_rows[np.maximum(hp - 1, 0)], 0)

import json,re,pandas as pd,numpy as np
from churn.extract import load_extract
from churn.visibility import _committed_transactions,_orders_rename_commit,_legacy_intervals,order_commit_times
D='/app/data'; ops=D+'/_ops'
T=load_extract(D); o=T['orders']; eff=order_commit_times(o,ops)
committed=_committed_transactions(ops); rename=_orders_rename_commit(ops,committed); intervals=_legacy_intervals(ops,committed,rename)
pat=re.compile(r'^\S+ legacy_orders run=\S+ selected orders where ordered_at >= (\S+) and ordered_at < (\S+): (\d+) rows; sent txn (\d+) to commit into (\S+)$')
rows=[]
for s in open(ops+'/scheduler.log'):
 m=pat.match(s.rstrip())
 if m and m.group(5)=='orders' and int(m.group(4)) in committed and int(m.group(3))>0 and committed[int(m.group(4))]<rename:
  rows.append((pd.Timestamp(m.group(1)).value,pd.Timestamp(m.group(2)).value,int(m.group(3)),int(m.group(4))))
z=pd.DataFrame(rows,columns=['start','end','selected','txn']).sort_values(['start','txn']).drop_duplicates('start')
loaded=o['_loaded_at'].to_numpy(dtype='datetime64[ns]').astype('int64'); event=o['ordered_at'].to_numpy(dtype='datetime64[ns]').astype('int64')
pre=event<int(rename); pos=np.searchsorted(z.start.to_numpy(),event[pre],side='right')-1; known=(pos>=0)&(event[pre]<z.end.to_numpy()[np.clip(pos,0,len(z)-1)])
idx=np.clip(pos,0,len(z)-1)
summary=pd.DataFrame({'txn':z.txn.iloc[idx[known]].to_numpy(),'selected':z.selected.iloc[idx[known]].to_numpy(),'event':event[pre][known],'eff':eff.to_numpy(dtype='datetime64[ns]').astype('int64')[pre][known]})
counts=summary.groupby('txn').size().rename('mapped'); sums=summary.groupby('txn').eff.min().rename('min_eff')
check=z.set_index('txn').join(counts).join(sums)
check['count_diff']=check.mapped-check.selected
print('rename',rename,'intervals',len(z),'pre-rename rows',pre.sum(),'known',known.sum(),'unmapped',(~known).sum())
print('count differences nonzero',int((check.count_diff!=0).sum()),'sum selected',int(check.selected.sum()),'sum mapped',int(check.mapped.sum()))
print(check[check.count_diff!=0].head(20).to_string())
print('visibility before event?',int((summary.min_eff<=summary.event).sum()),'of',len(summary))
